To minimize exposure.

Password gets hashed, because otherwise you may be leaking metadata that's critical, such as length of your password. That makes brute-force attacks way more powerful.

Password hash gets salted before hashing, because it helps prevent table attacks on the password.

Each session token is generated using a nonce, so that if your TLS session gets broken at some point the attacker can't reuse the already hashed token to impersonate you using a different session token.

TLS isn't entirely secure, but a big vulnerability is that your traffic may be intercepted and stored to be decrypted at a later date when your private key is acquired.

Summary: never send password over wire (even during registration, use a salted hash) don't reuse session tokens in case TLS gets broken. Use tls
